title: 10. NLP, Transformers & LLMs: Stage 3: Using Transformer Models
summary: This notebook covers how to use pre-trained transformer models for various NLP tasks: Text Classification; Named Entity Recognition (NER); Question Answering; Text Generation; Summarization & Translation

sections.title: Overview
sections.body:
This notebook covers how to use pre-trained transformer models for various NLP tasks:
- Text Classification
- Named Entity Recognition (NER)
- Question Answering
- Text Generation
- Summarization & Translation

Each section includes 5+ executable examples and exercises.

sections.title: 3.1 Model Loading & AutoClasses
sections.body:
### Architecture Overview
```
AutoModel Family:
├── AutoModel (base embeddings)
├── AutoModelForSequenceClassification
├── AutoModelForTokenClassification
├── AutoModelForQuestionAnswering
├── AutoModelForCausalLM (GPT-style)
└── AutoModelForSeq2SeqLM (BART, T5)
```

```python
# Install required packages
pip install transformers datasets torch accelerate -q
```

```python
# Example 1: Load base model for embeddings
from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer
import torch

model_name = "bert-base-uncased"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name)

# Get embeddings
text = "Transformers are powerful!"
inputs = tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt")
outputs = model(**inputs)

print(f"Last hidden state shape: {outputs.last_hidden_state.shape}")
print(f"Pooler output shape: {outputs.pooler_output.shape}")
```

```python
# Example 2: Compare different AutoModel variants
from transformers import AutoConfig

models_info = {
    "AutoModel": "Base model, returns embeddings",
    "AutoModelForSequenceClassification": "Text classification (sentiment, topic)",
    "AutoModelForTokenClassification": "Token-level tasks (NER, POS tagging)",
    "AutoModelForQuestionAnswering": "Extractive QA (SQuAD-style)",
    "AutoModelForCausalLM": "Text generation (GPT, Llama)",
    "AutoModelForSeq2SeqLM": "Seq2Seq tasks (BART, T5)"
}

for model_type, description in models_info.items():
    print(f"📦 {model_type}")
    print(f"   Use case: {description}\n")
```

```python
# Example 3: Load model with custom configuration
from transformers import AutoConfig, AutoModelForSequenceClassification

config = AutoConfig.from_pretrained(
    "distilbert-base-uncased",
    num_labels=3,  # Custom number of classes
    problem_type="single_label_classification",
    id2label={0: "negative", 1: "neutral", 2: "positive"},
    label2id={"negative": 0, "neutral": 1, "positive": 2}
)

model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(
    "distilbert-base-uncased",
    config=config,
    ignore_mismatched_sizes=True  # Reinitialize classifier head
)

print(f"Model config: {model.config.num_labels} labels")
print(f"Label mapping: {model.config.id2label}")
```

```python
# Example 4: Model information and architecture inspection
from transformers import AutoModel

model = AutoModel.from_pretrained("bert-base-uncased")

# Count parameters
total_params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())
trainable_params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad)

print(f"Total parameters: {total_params:,}")
print(f"Trainable parameters: {trainable_params:,}")
print(f"\nModel architecture:")
print(model)
```

```python
# Example 5: Load model in different precision modes
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM
import torch

# Full precision (FP32)
model_fp32 = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("gpt2")

# Half precision (FP16) - saves memory
model_fp16 = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    "gpt2",
    torch_dtype=torch.float16
)

# 8-bit quantization - requires bitsandbytes
# model_8bit = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
#     "gpt2",
#     load_in_8bit=True,
#     device_map="auto"
# )

print(f"FP32 model size: ~{sum(p.numel() * 4 for p in model_fp32.parameters()) / 1e6:.1f} MB")
print(f"FP16 model size: ~{sum(p.numel() * 2 for p in model_fp16.parameters()) / 1e6:.1f} MB")
```

sections.title: 3.2 Text Classification
sections.body:
### Task Overview
```
Text → Tokenizer → Model → Classification Head → Probabilities
"Great movie!" → [101, 2307, ...] → BERT → Linear(768→2) → [0.1, 0.9]
```

```python
# Example 1: Sentiment Analysis with Pipeline
from transformers import pipeline

classifier = pipeline("sentiment-analysis")

texts = [
    "I absolutely loved this movie!",
    "This was the worst experience ever.",
    "It was okay, nothing special.",
    "Fantastic product, highly recommend!",
    "Terrible quality, waste of money."
]

results = classifier(texts)

for text, result in zip(texts, results):
    print(f"Text: {text}")
    print(f"Sentiment: {result['label']} (confidence: {result['score']:.3f})\n")
```

```python
# Example 2: Manual classification with softmax
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForSequenceClassification
import torch

model_name = "distilbert-base-uncased-finetuned-sst-2-english"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(model_name)

text = "This movie exceeded all my expectations!"
inputs = tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt", padding=True, truncation=True)

# Get predictions
with torch.no_grad():
    outputs = model(**inputs)
    logits = outputs.logits
    probabilities = torch.softmax(logits, dim=1)

predicted_class = torch.argmax(probabilities, dim=1).item()

print(f"Text: {text}")
print(f"Logits: {logits}")
print(f"Probabilities: {probabilities}")
print(f"Predicted class: {model.config.id2label[predicted_class]}")
```

```python
# Example 3: Batch processing for efficiency
from transformers import pipeline

classifier = pipeline(
    "text-classification",
    model="cardiffnlp/twitter-roberta-base-sentiment",
    device=0 if torch.cuda.is_available() else -1  # Use GPU if available
)

# Batch of tweets
tweets = [
    "Just got promoted! Best day ever! 🎉",
    "Can't believe they cancelled my favorite show 😢",
    "Weather is nice today",
    "This traffic is absolutely terrible!",
    "Love spending time with family ❤️"
]

# Process in batch (faster than one-by-one)
results = classifier(tweets, batch_size=8, truncation=True)

for tweet, result in zip(tweets, results):
    print(f"Tweet: {tweet}")
    print(f"Sentiment: {result['label']} ({result['score']:.2%})\n")
```

```python
# Example 4: Multi-label classification
from transformers import pipeline

# Multi-label classifier (one text can have multiple labels)
classifier = pipeline(
    "text-classification",
    model="cardiffnlp/tweet-topic-21-multi",
    top_k=None  # Return all labels with scores
)

text = "Breaking: New AI model achieves state-of-the-art results in natural language understanding!"
results = classifier(text)[0]  # Returns list of all labels

# Filter and sort by confidence
top_labels = sorted(results, key=lambda x: x['score'], reverse=True)[:3]

print(f"Text: {text}\n")
print("Top 3 topics:")
for label_info in top_labels:
    print(f"  {label_info['label']}: {label_info['score']:.2%}")
```

```python
# Example 5: Zero-shot classification (no fine-tuning needed!)
from transformers import pipeline

classifier = pipeline("zero-shot-classification", model="facebook/bart-large-mnli")

text = "The stock market crashed today, causing panic among investors."
candidate_labels = ["business", "sports", "technology", "politics", "entertainment"]

result = classifier(text, candidate_labels, multi_label=False)

print(f"Text: {text}\n")
print("Classification scores:")
for label, score in zip(result['labels'], result['scores']):
    print(f"  {label}: {score:.2%}")
```

sections.title: 3.3 Named Entity Recognition (NER)
sections.body:
### Task Overview
```
Token-level classification:
Text: "Apple was founded by Steve Jobs in California"
Tags: [O, B-ORG, O, O, O, B-PER, I-PER, O, B-LOC]
```

```python
# Example 1: Basic NER with pipeline
from transformers import pipeline

ner = pipeline("ner", model="dslim/bert-base-NER", aggregation_strategy="simple")

text = "Apple was founded by Steve Jobs in Cupertino, California. Tim Cook is the current CEO."
entities = ner(text)

print(f"Text: {text}\n")
print("Entities found:")
for entity in entities:
    print(f"  {entity['word']}: {entity['entity_group']} (confidence: {entity['score']:.2%})")
```

```python
# Example 2: Manual NER with token classification
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForTokenClassification
import torch

model_name = "dslim/bert-base-NER"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
model = AutoModelForTokenClassification.from_pretrained(model_name)

text = "Elon Musk founded SpaceX in 2002."
inputs = tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt")

with torch.no_grad():
    outputs = model(**inputs)
    predictions = torch.argmax(outputs.logits, dim=2)

# Map predictions to labels
tokens = tokenizer.convert_ids_to_tokens(inputs["input_ids"][0])
predicted_labels = [model.config.id2label[pred.item()] for pred in predictions[0]]

print(f"Text: {text}\n")
print("Token-level predictions:")
for token, label in zip(tokens, predicted_labels):
    if token not in ['[CLS]', '[SEP]', '[PAD]']:
        print(f"  {token:15} → {label}")
```

```python
# Example 3: Biomedical NER (domain-specific)
from transformers import pipeline

# Specialized model for medical entities
ner_bio = pipeline(
    "ner",
    model="d4data/biomedical-ner-all",
    aggregation_strategy="simple"
)

medical_text = "The patient was diagnosed with diabetes mellitus and prescribed metformin 500mg."
entities = ner_bio(medical_text)

print(f"Medical text: {medical_text}\n")
print("Extracted entities:")
for entity in entities:
    print(f"  {entity['word']}: {entity['entity_group']} ({entity['score']:.2%})")
```

```python
# Example 4: Entity extraction and grouping
from transformers import pipeline
from collections import defaultdict

ner = pipeline("ner", model="dslim/bert-base-NER", aggregation_strategy="simple")

text = """Microsoft was founded by Bill Gates and Paul Allen in Seattle. 
The company is now led by Satya Nadella from their headquarters in Redmond, Washington."""

entities = ner(text)

# Group by entity type
grouped = defaultdict(list)
for entity in entities:
    grouped[entity['entity_group']].append(entity['word'])

print(f"Text: {text}\n")
print("Entities by type:")
for entity_type, words in grouped.items():
    print(f"  {entity_type}: {', '.join(words)}")
```

```python
# Example 5: NER with confidence thresholding
from transformers import pipeline

ner = pipeline("ner", model="dslim/bert-base-NER", aggregation_strategy="simple")

text = "Google's CEO Sundar Pichai announced new AI features at the conference in San Francisco."
entities = ner(text)

# Filter by confidence threshold
confidence_threshold = 0.9
high_confidence = [e for e in entities if e['score'] >= confidence_threshold]
low_confidence = [e for e in entities if e['score'] < confidence_threshold]

print(f"Text: {text}\n")
print(f"High confidence entities (≥{confidence_threshold:.0%}):")
for entity in high_confidence:
    print(f"  {entity['word']}: {entity['entity_group']} ({entity['score']:.2%})")

print(f"\nLow confidence entities (<{confidence_threshold:.0%}):")
for entity in low_confidence:
    print(f"  {entity['word']}: {entity['entity_group']} ({entity['score']:.2%})")
```

sections.title: 3.5 Text Generation
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- Example 1: Basic text generation with GPT-2
- Example 2: Generation with different decoding strategies
- Example 3: Controlled generation with parameters
- Conservative generation (low temperature, high top_p)
- Creative generation (high temperature, lower top_p)
- Example 4: Constrained generation with stopping criteria
- Stop when we generate a period
- Example 5: Beam search for better quality

### Task Overview
```
Causal Language Modeling (GPT-style):
Input: "Once upon a time"
Output: "Once upon a time there was a brave knight..."
```

```python
# Example 1: Basic text generation with GPT-2
from transformers import pipeline

generator = pipeline("text-generation", model="gpt2")

prompt = "The future of artificial intelligence is"
results = generator(
    prompt,
    max_length=50,
    num_return_sequences=3,
    temperature=0.8
)

print(f"Prompt: {prompt}\n")
for i, result in enumerate(results, 1):
    print(f"Generation {i}:")
    print(result['generated_text'])
    print()
```

```python
# Example 2: Generation with different decoding strategies
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM
import torch

model_name = "gpt2"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_name)

prompt = "To be or not to be,"
inputs = tokenizer(prompt, return_tensors="pt")

# Greedy decoding (deterministic)
greedy_output = model.generate(**inputs, max_length=30, do_sample=False)
print("Greedy decoding:")
print(tokenizer.decode(greedy_output[0], skip_special_tokens=True))
print()

# Sampling with temperature
sample_output = model.generate(**inputs, max_length=30, do_sample=True, temperature=0.7)
print("Sampling (temp=0.7):")
print(tokenizer.decode(sample_output[0], skip_special_tokens=True))
print()

# Top-k sampling
topk_output = model.generate(**inputs, max_length=30, do_sample=True, top_k=50)
print("Top-k sampling (k=50):")
print(tokenizer.decode(topk_output[0], skip_special_tokens=True))
print()

# Top-p (nucleus) sampling
topp_output = model.generate(**inputs, max_length=30, do_sample=True, top_p=0.9)
print("Top-p sampling (p=0.9):")
print(tokenizer.decode(topp_output[0], skip_special_tokens=True))
```

```python
# Example 3: Controlled generation with parameters
from transformers import pipeline

generator = pipeline("text-generation", model="gpt2")

prompt = "In a world where robots"

# Conservative generation (low temperature, high top_p)
conservative = generator(
    prompt,
    max_length=40,
    temperature=0.3,
    top_p=0.95,
    repetition_penalty=1.2
)

print("Conservative (predictable):")
print(conservative[0]['generated_text'])
print()

# Creative generation (high temperature, lower top_p)
creative = generator(
    prompt,
    max_length=40,
    temperature=1.5,
    top_p=0.85,
    repetition_penalty=1.2
)

print("Creative (diverse):")
print(creative[0]['generated_text'])
```

```python
# Example 4: Constrained generation with stopping criteria
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM, StoppingCriteria, StoppingCriteriaList
import torch

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("gpt2")
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("gpt2")

# Custom stopping criteria
class StopOnPeriod(StoppingCriteria):
    def __call__(self, input_ids, scores, **kwargs):
        # Stop when we generate a period
        period_token = tokenizer.encode('.', add_special_tokens=False)[0]
        return period_token in input_ids[0]

prompt = "The three laws of robotics are:"
inputs = tokenizer(prompt, return_tensors="pt")

outputs = model.generate(
    **inputs,
    max_length=100,
    stopping_criteria=StoppingCriteriaList([StopOnPeriod()])
)

print("Generation (stops at first period):")
print(tokenizer.decode(outputs[0], skip_special_tokens=True))
```

```python
# Example 5: Beam search for better quality
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("gpt2")
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("gpt2")

prompt = "The key to happiness is"
inputs = tokenizer(prompt, return_tensors="pt")

# Beam search (explores multiple paths)
beam_output = model.generate(
    **inputs,
    max_length=40,
    num_beams=5,
    num_return_sequences=3,
    early_stopping=True
)

print(f"Prompt: {prompt}\n")
print("Top 3 beam search results:")
for i, output in enumerate(beam_output, 1):
    print(f"{i}. {tokenizer.decode(output, skip_special_tokens=True)}")
    print()
```

sections.title: 3.6 Summarization & Translation
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- Artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming industries across the globe.
- The James Webb Space Telescope has captured stunning images of distant galaxies.
- Climate change is one of the most pressing challenges facing humanity.
- Example 1: Text summarization with BART
- Example 2: Abstractive vs extractive summarization
- Abstractive (generates new text)
- Example 3: Translation with MarianMT
- Example 4: Multilingual translation with mBART

### Task Overview
```
Seq2Seq Tasks (BART, T5):
Summarization: Long text → Short summary
Translation: Source language → Target language
```

```python
# Example 1: Text summarization with BART
from transformers import pipeline

summarizer = pipeline("summarization", model="facebook/bart-large-cnn")

article = """Artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming industries across the globe. 
From healthcare to finance, AI systems are being deployed to automate tasks, analyze data, and make predictions. 
Machine learning algorithms can now diagnose diseases, detect fraud, and even drive cars autonomously. 
However, the rise of AI also brings challenges, including ethical concerns about bias, privacy, and job displacement. 
Researchers and policymakers are working to develop frameworks that ensure AI is developed and used responsibly. 
The future of AI depends on striking a balance between innovation and regulation."""

summary = summarizer(article, max_length=60, min_length=30, do_sample=False)

print("Original article:")
print(article)
print(f"\nSummary ({len(summary[0]['summary_text'].split())} words):")
print(summary[0]['summary_text'])
```

```python
# Example 2: Abstractive vs extractive summarization
from transformers import pipeline

# Abstractive (generates new text)
abstractive = pipeline("summarization", model="facebook/bart-large-cnn")

text = """The James Webb Space Telescope has captured stunning images of distant galaxies. 
Scientists are using these images to study the early universe and understand how galaxies formed. 
The telescope's advanced infrared capabilities allow it to see through cosmic dust and observe objects 
that are billions of light-years away."""

abs_summary = abstractive(text, max_length=40, min_length=20)

print("Original text:")
print(text)
print("\nAbstractive summary (new phrasing):")
print(abs_summary[0]['summary_text'])
```

```python
# Example 3: Translation with MarianMT
from transformers import pipeline

# English to French
en_to_fr = pipeline("translation", model="Helsinki-NLP/opus-mt-en-fr")
en_text = "Hello, how are you? I hope you're having a great day!"
fr_translation = en_to_fr(en_text)

print("English:", en_text)
print("French:", fr_translation[0]['translation_text'])
print()

# English to Spanish
en_to_es = pipeline("translation", model="Helsinki-NLP/opus-mt-en-es")
es_translation = en_to_es(en_text)

print("Spanish:", es_translation[0]['translation_text'])
print()

# English to German
en_to_de = pipeline("translation", model="Helsinki-NLP/opus-mt-en-de")
de_translation = en_to_de(en_text)

print("German:", de_translation[0]['translation_text'])
```

```python
# Example 4: Multilingual translation with mBART
from transformers import MBartForConditionalGeneration, MBart50TokenizerFast

model = MBartForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained("facebook/mbart-large-50-many-to-many-mmt")
tokenizer = MBart50TokenizerFast.from_pretrained("facebook/mbart-large-50-many-to-many-mmt")

# Translate from English to multiple languages
text = "Transformers are revolutionizing natural language processing."

# English to French
tokenizer.src_lang = "en_XX"
encoded = tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt")
generated = model.generate(**encoded, forced_bos_token_id=tokenizer.lang_code_to_id["fr_XX"])
fr_text = tokenizer.decode(generated[0], skip_special_tokens=True)

print("English:", text)
print("French:", fr_text)
print()

# English to Chinese
generated = model.generate(**encoded, forced_bos_token_id=tokenizer.lang_code_to_id["zh_CN"])
zh_text = tokenizer.decode(generated[0], skip_special_tokens=True)

print("Chinese:", zh_text)
```

```python
# Example 5: Custom summarization with T5
from transformers import pipeline

# T5 uses task prefixes
t5_summarizer = pipeline("summarization", model="t5-small")

article = """Climate change is one of the most pressing challenges facing humanity. 
Rising global temperatures are causing ice caps to melt, sea levels to rise, and extreme weather events to become more frequent. 
Scientists agree that human activities, particularly the burning of fossil fuels, are the primary cause. 
Governments and organizations worldwide are working to reduce carbon emissions and transition to renewable energy sources. 
Individual actions, such as reducing energy consumption and supporting sustainable practices, also play a crucial role."""

# Different summary lengths
short_summary = t5_summarizer(article, max_length=30, min_length=10)
medium_summary = t5_summarizer(article, max_length=60, min_length=30)
long_summary = t5_summarizer(article, max_length=100, min_length=50)

print("Original:", len(article.split()), "words\n")
print("Short summary:", short_summary[0]['summary_text'])
print("\nMedium summary:", medium_summary[0]['summary_text'])
print("\nLong summary:", long_summary[0]['summary_text'])
```
